Check keys and duplicate rows

Source: R/keys.R
keys.Rd

Stata-style checks of identifying variables and duplicated rows.

  • isid() checks that the selected columns uniquely identify the rows, like Stata's isid. It returns the data invisibly when they do and errors otherwise, so it can sit inside a pipeline. Wrap it in capture() for a TRUE/FALSE answer.

  • duplicates_report() counts how many rows share the same values, like duplicates report.

  • duplicates_tag() adds the number of other rows with the same values, like duplicates tag, generate().

  • duplicates_list() returns the duplicated rows, like duplicates list.

  • duplicates_drop() keeps the first row of each duplicated set, like duplicates drop.

Usage

isid(.data, ..., .missok = FALSE)

duplicates_report(.data, ...)

duplicates_tag(.data, ..., .name = "dup")

duplicates_list(.data, ...)

duplicates_drop(.data, ..., .force = FALSE)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

<tidy-select> The identifying columns. Omit to use all columns, as Stata does.

.missok

A single TRUE or FALSE. If FALSE (default), isid() errors when an identifying column contains missing values, as Stata's isid does without the missok option.

.name

Name of the new column created by duplicates_tag().

.force

A single TRUE or FALSE. When only some columns are selected, rows that share those columns can still differ elsewhere, and duplicates_drop() errors unless .force = TRUE, like Stata's duplicates drop varlist, force.

Value

  • isid(): .data, invisibly.

  • duplicates_report(): a tibble with one row per number of copies: copies, observations (rows with that many copies) and surplus (rows beyond the first of each set).

  • duplicates_tag(): .data with an integer column of the number of other rows sharing the same values (0 for unique rows).

  • duplicates_list(): the duplicated rows, ordered by their identifying values, with .dup_group (set number) and .row (original position). Existing columns with either metadata name cause an error; rename them first.

  • duplicates_drop(): .data without the surplus rows, with a message giving the number of rows removed.

The input's data.frame, tibble, data.table or grouped container is kept where rows or columns of .data are returned.

Details

Missing values count as equal to each other, as in Stata, so two rows that are both missing on every selected column are duplicates.

See also

Other data checking functions: assert(), is_first(), stata_merge()

Examples

panel <- tibble::tibble(
  id = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3),
  wave = c(1, 2, 1, 1, 1),
  score = c(5, 6, 7, 7, 8)
)
# id repeats, so this errors; capture() turns it into TRUE/FALSE
try(isid(panel, id))
#> Error in isid(panel, id) : 
#>   Variable `id` does not uniquely identify the rows: 2 values appear more
#> than once (4 rows).
#> ℹ See them with `duplicates_list()`.
capture(isid(panel, id))
#> [1] FALSE
isid(panel[-4, ], id, wave)

duplicates_report(panel, id, wave)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   copies observations surplus
#>    <int>        <int>   <int>
#> 1      1            3       0
#> 2      2            2       1
duplicates_tag(panel, id, wave)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>      id  wave score   dup
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <int>
#> 1     1     1     5     0
#> 2     1     2     6     0
#> 3     2     1     7     1
#> 4     2     1     7     1
#> 5     3     1     8     0
duplicates_list(panel, id, wave)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>      id  wave score .dup_group  .row
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>      <int> <int>
#> 1     2     1     7          1     3
#> 2     2     1     7          1     4
duplicates_drop(panel)
#> (1 row removed)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>      id  wave score
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1     1     5
#> 2     1     2     6
#> 3     2     1     7
#> 4     3     1     8
